items.summary:
Artificial Analysis 和 Google DeepMind 联合发布 MKA 基准，用 200 个视觉任务测 AI 做知识工作

MKA 的输入是建筑图纸、工程示意图、临床扫描这类视觉复杂的项目文件，要求代理产出幻灯片、表格、PDF、Word 文档和标记过的图片。任务来自 10 个行业，都是私有的真实任务。

评分分两类：Regression 是模型应当通过的基础检查，Climb 是更难、用来拉开差距的检查；每条任务约 70 条加权标准，榜单看的是 Climb WSR（Climb 标准的加权完成比例）。

Claude Fable 5.2 以 57% 的 Climb WSR 领先，Gemini 4 Carbon 54%，Claude Opus 5.5 53%。但 Fable 5.2 每个任务平均花 31.97 美元，是 Carbon 的 5 倍多，只换来约 2 个百分点；是 GPT-6.1 Sol（1.11 美元）的近 29 倍。没有任何一个模型在全部 10 个行业里都领先。

items.title: **Perplexity Computer** 是 Perplexity 推出的自主 AI 数字工作者（agent 平台），核心定位是“做工作”而不是“回答问题”。[](<https://t.co/a4iuF7iCoQ>)
items.summary:
**Perplexity Computer** 是 Perplexity 推出的自主 AI 数字工作者（agent 平台），核心定位是“做工作”而不是“回答问题”。[](<https://t.co/a4iuF7iCoQ>)

普通 Perplexity 负责搜索和知识综合；Computer 则负责**执行完整工作流**：你描述一个目标（outcome），它会自动拆解任务、调用多个专业子代理、操作工具、生成成果，并在后台持续运行（可长达数小时甚至数月）。[](<https://t.co/cpzkFn44hC>)

### 主要能做什么

- **多步骤工作流自动化**：例如“研究前 5 名竞争对手的定价，做成 PPT，并邮件发给团队”——它会并行搜索、分析、生成文档并直接发送。[](<https://t.co/a4iuF7iCoQ>)
- **研究与分析**：深度市场调研、竞争分析、财务分析、数据提取与可视化（可生成报告、仪表盘、表格等）。
- **内容与资产创建**：撰写文档、制作演示文稿、生成图表/图像/视频、构建可运行的应用或网站。
- **工具与应用集成**：连接 400+ 应用（Gmail、Outlook、Slack、Notion、GitHub、Linear、Salesforce、Snowflake 等），可读写邮件、管理日历、操作项目工具、拉取企业数据。
- **调度与持续运行**：设置定时任务、条件触发（如监控邮件/日历/航班）、后台异步执行，支持“早间简报”“截止日期提醒”等。
- **多模型编排**：自动调度 15–20+ 个前沿模型（Claude、Gemini、GPT、Grok 等），为不同子任务选择最合适的模型。
- **其他能力**：浏览器自动化、代码编写与执行、持久记忆（跨会话记住上下文和偏好）、在隔离沙箱中安全运行。

### 版本与使用方式

- **云端 Computer**（网页/应用）：主版本，在 Perplexity 安全沙箱中运行。
- **Personal Computer**（Mac/Windows 桌面应用）：可访问本地文件、原生应用（如 Notes、Mail、Finder、Office），支持语音控制，适合个人工作流；也可在支持的硬件上完全本地运行。
- **Enterprise 版本**：面向团队，连接企业数据源（Snowflake、Salesforce 等）。
- **其他扩展**：Teammates（持久专属代理）、通过邮件发送任务、技能（Skills）与插件系统等。

它面向 Pro 和 Max 订阅用户（Max 用户获得更多 credits），部分免费账户有有限试用次数。最近还集成了 Gemini 4 Carbon 等新模型，用于更强的长周期研究任务。

简单说：**Chat 给答案，Agent 做任务，Computer 直接把活干完并交付成果**。

items.title: AI100 Report: AI has entered the mainstream and is reshaping society | Max-Planck-Gesellschaft
items.summary:
1. Scaling is the paradigm that has powered the chief advances in generative AI over the last five years: building AI systems using ever more compute and ever more data. But the scaling paradigm is running into data and compute constraints, shifting the frontier toward reasoning and inference-time compute.
2. Like the World Wide Web, AI is a disruptive technology. It is already transforming the creative industries, mathematics, and software development, all fields that believed themselves beyond its reach. They join a long list of sectors upended by technology over the past 30 years, from journalism and the music industry to retail. Other areas that believe themselves immune from AI also stand to be disrupted in short order. [...] Artificial intelligence has moved from a specialised technology to an everyday reality for millions of people. According to the latest report from the One Hundred Year Study on Artificial Intelligence (AI100), the past five years have marked a watershed moment in AI's development, driven by advances in large-scale computing, vast datasets, and the rapid rise of generative AI. The report, AI Goes Mainstream: The Scaling Era and the Rise of Generative AI, was released by AI100, a longitudinal project administered by Stanford University's Institute for Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence (HAI). Published every five years, the study examines AI's development and its impact on people, communities, and society across technical, ethical, economic, and societal domains. [...] 3. AI is transforming science at remarkable speed, a fact recognized by the 2024 Nobel Prizes in both Physics and Chemistry. It is compressing research timescales that used to be measured in years down to months or weeks, yet it also raises many new scientific grand challenges that demand attention.
4. Capital investment in AI infrastructure is unprecedented in scale and speed, propping up parts of the U.S. economy, dominating capital markets, fuelling fears of a financial bubble, and straining energy and freshwater supplies.
5. Frontier AI development is concentrated among a small number of U.S. and Chinese actors, raising international concerns about who will ultimately own and have access to leading-edge AI technologies.

items.title: Artificial intelligence is desperately seeking its narrative
items.summary:
Four broad narratives currently shape the discourse on artificial intelligence. They are neither mutually exclusive nor entirely coherent: the same company or executive may embrace several, sometimes contradictory, visions.

## Narrative No. 1: ‘AI will save us… if it does not destroy us’

The first narrative presents AI as a civilisational gamble: it could usher in unprecedented abundance and scientific progress, but also trigger catastrophes or escape human control.

In September 2024, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman envisioned AI accelerating scientific discovery, solving complex problems and making capabilities once reserved for specialists widely accessible. [...] In July 2026, Le Monde diplomatique declared that “The AI backlash has begun”. The initial sense of wonder generated by ChatGPT has increasingly given way to broader public unease about AI’s social consequences, from its effects on work, education and information to concerns about privacy, the environment and the growing power of technology companies. In this emerging narrative, AI appears as a “digital Moloch” whose costs are borne collectively while its benefits accrue to only a handful of oligarchs. [...] China’s official discourse, for example, offers a revealing contrast. It does not herald the arrival of a superintelligence that will either save humanity or bring about an apocalypse. Instead, it describes the methodical integration of AI into the real economy through a proactive industrial policy and under state control. This model raises other questions, particularly concerning political centralisation, surveillance and freedom of expression, but it reminds us that the American imagination of AI is not the only possible one.

items.title: AMA: Artificial intelligence can augment physicians but don’t call it doctor | American Medical Association
items.summary:
ORLANDO — The American Medical Association (AMA) is drawing a clear line between artificial intelligence as a tool to support healthcare and the practice of medicine: AI can augment physicians and assist with clinical tasks, but it cannot be granted physician licensure, professional titles or certification to practice medicine.

Adopted Monday at the AMA’s Interim Meeting, the policy calls for AI-enabled technologies to be integrated into physician-led teams and used at the direction of the treating physician. AI tools used for clinical functions such as diagnosis, prescribing and care management should have transparent, auditable evidence demonstrating their safety and efficacy and be subject to appropriate regulation, documentation and liability requirements. [...] The AMA will advocate for legislation establishing a framework for physician oversight of AI clinical decision-making, including protections for physicians' independent clinical judgment and against liability for choosing not to use an AI tool or follow an AI recommendation.

“AI can help physicians analyze information, identify patterns and support clinical decision-making, but patients deserve to know who is responsible for their care,” said AMA President Willie Underwood III, MD, MSc, MPH. “Physicians also need the authority, oversight and liability protections to make independent decisions when AI is part of the care team.” [...] When errors stem from defective clinical AI products, the policy says liability should rest with vendors, manufacturers or distributors rather than physicians facing medical malpractice claims. It also urges legislation requiring AI companies to carry adequate liability insurance, disclose product limitations and performance data, and prohibit vendor contracts from shifting responsibility for product failures onto physicians or health systems.

When hospitals, health systems, insurers or other entities require the use of specific AI products, those organizations and the AI vendors should bear responsibility when errors from those mandated products cause patient harm.

results.input: Giải giúp mình bài toán tích phân: nguyên hàm của x^2 là gì?

result.actual_text:
Nguyên hàm của $x^2$ là:

$$\frac{x^3}{3} + C$$

(trong đó $C$ là hằng số tích phân).

Cách tính: Dùng quy tắc mũ cho tích phân:
$$\int x^n \, dx = \frac{x^{n+1}}{n+1} + C$$
Với $n = 2$:
$$\int x^2 \, dx = \frac{x^{2+1}}{2+1} + C = \frac{x^3}{3} + C$$

items.title: Who can be licensed as a physician? Not AI | American Medical Association
items.summary: The AMA is drawing a clear line between augmented intelligence (AI) as a tool to support healthcare and the practice of medicine. AI—often called artificial intelligence—can help doctors with clinical tasks, but it cannot be granted physician licensure, professional titles or certification to practice medicine, says new policy adopted at the 2026 AMA Interim Meeting. [...] “AI can help physicians analyze information, identify patterns and support clinical decision-making, but patients deserve to know who is responsible for their care,” said AMA President Willie Underwood III, MD, MSc, MPH. “Physicians also need the authority, oversight and liability protections to make independent decisions when AI is part of the care team.” [...] Transparency and physician-led oversight are needed as hospitals and health systems increasingly incorporate augmented intelligence (AI) into administrative and governance workflows, as well as emerging applications that support credentialing, privileging, peer review, quality review and other professional practices evaluation processes, says a separate resolution that was introduced at the 2026 AMA Interim Meeting.

items.title: Anthropic to raise $64bn in major stock market listing
items.summary:
# Anthropic to raise $64bn in major stock market listing

Getty Images Claude by Anthropic logo on a smartphone 

Anthropic, the AI company behind the Claude chatbot, is planning to raise up to $64bn (£48bn) when it lists its shares for sale on New York's Nasdaq stock exchange.

The loss-making company said it will offer its shares for between $70 and $78 each in its initial public offering (IPO), which is expected to go ahead this month. [...] Fiona Cincotta, a senior market analyst at City Index, said the amount Anthropic wants to raise is "fairly bullish" within "the volatility [and] concerns towards AI that we've seen in sort of particularly last week".

She told Reuters: "It's showing that they are still sort of upbeat about the outlook as far as AI is concerned and that obviously that they think that the demand is going to be there."

## Global stocks plunge as fears over US AI slowdown spread to Asia and Europe [...] This would value Anthropic at between $1.1 trillion and $1.3 trillion which, although large, is below the $2 trillion some analysts had predicted weeks ago.

It is floating at a volatile time for AI firms. After last week's US midterm elections, the Nasdaq fell sharply on concerns a Democrat-led Congress could slow development of AI and the buildout of data centres.

There are also wider fears over the billions of dollars being spent on AI and whether it will pay off.

items.title: Jensen Huang’s Apology May Be the Only Correct Use of AI - The Atlantic
items.summary:
People (me) are always saying about AI, “This is a solution looking for a problem!” and “Who would possibly want to delegate things like knowing information about your childrenor creating works of art to a third-party series of zeroes and ones?” But there are some things in life that nobody wants to do, such as get a root canal, amputate a limb, or deal with your cable provider. Or, perhaps, apologize simultaneously to your employees and your wife of 40 years for jeopardizing your business and [...] Look, I just want to say that if NVIDIA CEO and reported spy-plot target Jensen Huang did get help from AI to write an apology email to his family and company about his affair (he’s said he uses AI to help write all of his first drafts), this might be the one use of AI that makes sense to me. [...] Now I am worried, based on Jensen Huang’s claim that this was “completely normal and not unusual” and an NVIDIA spokesperson’s insistence that his interactions with the alleged spy were “not unusual” that, actually, we’ll be seeing multiple emails like this. Finally, organic demand for AI! If so, the template will get better and better—that is, if we can still use the chips.

results.input: Viết giúp mình một hàm Python tính Fibonacci bằng recursion.

result.actual_text:
Here's a clean, standard recursive Fibonacci function in Python:

```python
def fibonacci(n):
    """Return the n-th Fibonacci number (0-indexed).
    
    fibonacci(0) = 0
    fibonacci(1) = 1
    fibonacci(n) = fibonacci(n-1) + fibonacci(n-2) for n > 1
    """
    if n <= 0:
        return 0
    elif n == 1:
        return 1
    else:
        return fibonacci(n - 1) + fibonacci(n - 2)


# Quick demo: print the first 10 Fibonacci numbers
for i in range(10):
    print(f"fibonacci({i}) = {fibonacci(i)}")
```

**Output:**
```
fibonacci(0) = 0
fibonacci(1) = 1
fibonacci(2) = 1
fibonacci(3) = 2
fibonacci(4) = 3
fibonacci(5) = 5
fibonacci(6) = 8
fibonacci(7) = 13
fibonacci(8) = 21
fibonacci(9) = 34
```

⚠️ **Note:** This naive recursion has exponential time complexity `O(2^n)`, so it becomes very slow for `n > ~30`. For production use, consider memoization (`functools.lru_cache`) or an iterative approach. Let me know if you'd like those versions too!

items.title: Gemini Robotics 2.5: Accelerating Physical Intelligence — Google DeepMind
items.summary:
Dexterity: Our robots can perform significantly more tasks with greater performance and dexterity — from using everyday tools to handling delicate, flexible objects.
 Reliability: During a real-world proof-of-concept on Mercedes-Benz production lines, our models helped Apptronik’s Apollo 2 humanoid pick and pack automotive parts with a 96% success rate. This could enable robots to take on monotonous work, to enable technicians to focus on complex build tasks. [...] Robots struggle to adapt to new unpredictable environments, our Gemini Robotics models give Apollo the ability to think, reason over multiple steps, and take action adapting to changes. In this proof-of-concept, Apollo 2 autonomously performs automotive kitting: the repetitive, physically taxing task of sorting individual parts from bulk bins into organized trays in the exact order needed for each vehicle on the line. Offloading this monotonous prep work helps keep the assembly line moving, [...] With Gemini Robotics 2.5, we expanded the model capabilities in task breadth, performance, and complexity. We evaluated the model across 200 distinct tasks — such as serving food with tongs, tying a bow on a gift box, and pipetting a liquid. These tasks represent a step toward human-level dexterity by combining a number of skills, including advanced tool use, complex manipulation of deformables, and handling delicate objects with finesse.

items.title: DeepMind reveals Gemini Robotics 2.5 and open safety benchmark "ASIMOV-jailbreak" - Ars Technica
items.summary: DeepMind says that Gemini Robotics 2.5 is much better at tasks that require a high degree of dexterity. The model was evaluated across more than 200 activities, including serving food with tongs and using a pipette, as you would see in a laboratory. Google also showed that Apptronik’s Apollo 2 humanoid robot with Gemini Robotics 2.5 can now tie a bow with its five-fingered hands, a notable feat, because deformable objects (like ribbon) are notoriously difficult for robots to manipulate. [...] Google DeepMind has revealed a new generation of the AI-powered Gemini Robotics platform. In the 2.5 release, Google says its robotic AI is getting tantalizingly close to completing real-world tasks as well as humans do. In fact, some Gemini robots were able to get actual work done in Mercedes-Benz factories, and the team is preparing for a day when robots operate alongside humans with an open source safety benchmark. [...] Overall, Gemini Robotics 2.5 manages a 30 to 100 percent higher success rate compared to the last version. It’s also 20 to 30 percent faster. But that’s based on laboratory testing. Google partnered with Apptronik and Mercedes-Benz to see how capable this AI is when faced with the uncertainty of the world outside robotics labs. The Gemini-powered Apollo 2 robots kitted automotive parts in a few European factories, reaching a 96 percent success rate.

items.title: Exclusive: OpenAI targets Microsoft's GitHub with deal
items.summary:
OpenAI will acquire Pierre Computer, a developer tools startup whose technology is already embedded in Codex, the company told Axios exclusively.

Why it matters:OpenAI is joining a slew of companies challenging Microsoft's GitHub as AI agents take on more coding work. The platform has acted as a central repository and nerve center for software development for many years.

Zoom out:GitHub has faced a number of reliability issues and outages as AI coding has taken off. [...] Financial terms were not disclosed. Pierre's open-source projects will remain open-source.

Between the lines:Earlier this week, OpenAI revealed Pando, built to handle the explosion of code generated by AI agents.

   OpenAI says Pando reduced the time needed to push code changes by nearly 80%. 
   The company is now exploring ways to make the technology available to customers. [...] Cursor, now owned by Elon Musk's SpaceX, launched GitHub rival Origin in August.
   Former GitHub CEO Thomas Dohmke, who launched a new coding startup, announced a competing product last month.
   Microsoft owns nearly a quarter of OpenAI, although the two companies also compete in a variety of ways, a dynamic that is common across the competitive AI landscape.

Driving the news: OpenAI plans to integrate Pierre's Code Storage function into Codex, where Pierre's technology is already used.
